title: Flex Commit Wallet + Spot Offset Pricing prototype
body:
Purpose
---
This working doc sketches a hybrid pricing construct intended to increase effective utilization of reserved GPU pools while preserving predictable revenue for Redwood Dedicated customers. The core idea: allow customers to buy a baseline commit bucket and an on-demand "wallet" that automatically offsets spot/interruptible capacity and burst usage with preferential pricing. Wallet credits smooth monthly spend and let us rebalance idle risk across customers with explicit offset rules.

High-level goals
- Increase committed pool utilization by ~6–18% vs today for mid-size accounts (50–300 GPUs) without raising sticker rates.
- Maintain predictable MRR for Redwood by guaranteeing a minimum committed revenue floor per contract term.
- Give customers clear, PLG-friendly UX for balancing cost vs availability (wallet top-ups, opt-in spot offset).
- Provide simple heuristics for billing reconciliation and monthly settlement.

Key components (verbal)
1) Baseline Commit: customer purchases a reserved bucket (N GPUs equivalent) with standard committed price per GPU-hour. Baseline comes with SLO-backed capacity guarantee up to a baseline concurrency.
2) Flex Wallet: a pre-paid credit pool purchased at contract signing or monthly top-ups. Wallet credits are consumed when customer uses burst capacity beyond baseline or when we displace spot instances to honor availability. Credits are priced below baseline but above our marginal spot cost.
3) Spot Offset: When a customer opts-in, we run cheaper preemptible capacity to fill wallet consumption first; if wallet is exhausted, fallback to on-demand (higher priced) or deny burst depending on policy.
4) Settlement Rules: monthly reconciliation that tops up wallet based on agreed threshold and issues invoice adjustments for over/under consumption.

Proposed pricing math (simple model)
- Baseline price: P_base = $2.40 per GPU-hour (example)
- Wallet price: P_wallet = $1.65 per GPU-hour equivalent (pre-paid discount, non-refundable within month)
- Spot marginal cost (internal): C_spot = $0.65 per GPU-hour (our cloud cost for preemptible)
- Effective revenue per GPU-hour when wallet used = P_wallet * (1 - partner_rebate) but we count full wallet as revenue in MRR.
- If wallet consumption comes from our reclaimed idle (we run spot for other customers), we treat incremental cost = C_spot + orchestration_overhead ($0.20) => $0.85.

Example scenarios (monthly, 30-day month)
Customer A: 100 GPU baseline, avg utilization on baseline 65%, monthly baseline-hours = 100 * 24 * 30 * 0.65 = 46,800 GPU-hrs
- Baseline billed = 100 * 24 * 30 * P_base = 72,000 GPU-hrs * $2.40 = $172,800 (note: baseline price billed on committed size, regardless of utilization)
- Wallet purchased = 10 GPU-equivalent continuous for bursts => 10 * 24 * 30 = 7,200 GPU-hr credit at $1.65 => wallet invoice = $11,880
- If customer used 60% of wallet in month => wallet consumed = 4,320 hrs; we book $4,320 * $1.65 = $7,128 incremental recognized revenue; unused credit carried per contract rules or refunded per top-up setting.

Net effect: that customer increases effective utilization of the pool because bursts that would previously be covered by on-demand (higher cost and less predictable) now reserve pre-paid wallet capacity we can use to fill scheduler holes.

Simulated utilization impact (aggregate model)
- Model assumptions: pool idle fraction baseline = 20%; burst demand across customers correlated alpha=0.3; wallet adoption=30% of customers in cohort.
- Simple Monte Carlo (sheet sim) shows: with 30% adoption and wallet sized at 10% of committed, average effective pool utilization increases from 80% -> 86% (sensitivity 81–89% across different correlation assumptions). See linked spreadsheet for full sim.

Accounting / GAAP implications (notes)
- Wallet pre-pay is recognized ratably over the month as credits are consumed; unconsumed credits are revenue if contract says non-refundable monthly top-up. Need to coordinate with Finance for recognition policy (deferred revenue).
- For ARR/MRR reporting, baseline committed amounts should count toward committed ARR; wallet sold as monthly recurring line item if auto-topup set.

Operational considerations
- Metering: accurate per-customer per-GPU-hour metering must tag wallet-consumption vs baseline consumption vs spot fallback. Implementation requires tracing at the routing layer (route decision id) and linking billing events.
- Scheduler: scheduler must prefer fulfilling wallet consumption with preemptible capacity and only escalate to on-demand if wallet exhausted + customer has allowed fallback. This interacts with capacity forecasting and replenishment algorithms.
- Quotas / SLOs: define explicit SLO for wallet-backed bursts (e.g., 90% hit rate for burst requests up to wallet size).

Edge cases / open questions
- Unused wallet credits: auto-rollover vs refund. Rollover encourages adoption but complicates revenue recognition; refund increases churn risk.
- Cross-customer pooling: can we aggregate wallet credits across teams inside an org? Complexity for metering but attractive UX.
- Anti-abuse: customers may buy minimal baseline + massive wallet to game discounts; need guardrails (max wallet % of baseline without enterprise signoff).
- Contract term impact: deeper discounts if multi-year commit + wallet bundling? Likely yes; run elasticity experiment.

Experiment plan (short)
1) Internal sim: extend linked sheet to model 1,000-customer cohort with realistic burst traces (use historical SRE metrics for inter-arrival and burst sizes). Run sensitivity on wallet price, wallet size distribution, and adoption rate. Owner: Sanjay Rao. Due: 2025-11-24.
2) Small A/B pilot: 10 mid-market customers invited to opt into wallet pilot for 3 months with promotional wallet price (P_wallet_promo = $1.45). Measure bump in utilization and churn/CSAT impact. Owner: Leah Martinez + Solutions Eng. Target start: 2026-01-15.
3) Billing integration spike: build metric tags in billing events to mark wallet vs baseline consumption. Owner: Eng-billing + Platform. Spike timebox: 2 sprints.

Metrics to track
- Effective pool utilization change (week over week)
- Wallet adoption rate (pct of targeted customers)
- Revenue per GPU-hour (blended) vs forecast
- Wallet churn (unused rollover, refunds requested)
- Incident correlation (does wallet-driven preemptible use increase scheduling incidents?)

Quick open TODOs (practical)
- [ ] Align with Finance on revenue recognition guardrails (Marcus)
- [ ] Add elasticity curve to spreadsheet: wallet price vs adoption (Sanjay)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing one-pager describing wallet behavior and failure modes (Arielle)

Links / refs
- Simulation sheet (working): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-flex-wallet-sim (contains Monte Carlo, sensitivity tabs)
- Related Jira epic: ENG-PRJ-7624 (wallet metering + billing)
- Slack thread: #dedicated-pricing (proposal discussion)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a lightweight hybrid construct; main risk is added product complexity and accounting overhead. Focus feedback on whether we can get 6–12% utilization uplift with limited engineering work.
- If we proceed to pilot, the billing metering and contract language are gating items.

End of draft.
